name: Chechnya
summary_text: Chechnya operates outside the Russian federal legal framework in practice. In February 2017, Chechen law-enforcement and security officials launched an anti-gay purge, rounding up dozens of men, holding them in unofficial detention facilities (documented by name and location, including a secret prison in Argun), humiliating, starving, and torturing them, forcibly disappearing some, and returning others to families "barely alive from beatings" after captors exposed them and encouraged relatives to carry out honour killings (HRW, 2017). Novaya Gazeta reported in January 2019 that persecution had resumed and the Argun facility was "full again," while Kadyrov's press chief publicly denied any unofficial detention sites exist. The pattern has mutated and continues: North Caucasus SOS documented at least seven cases of Chechen security forces blackmailing detained homosexual men into "volunteering" for front-line conscription in Ukraine (one already killed), and Memorial found a mass wave of unlawful detentions tied to forced conscription. In 2021, Kadyrov's aide announced the abduction of two men evacuated abroad, taken at the Gudermes police station. The UK Home Office CPIN (June 2025) explicitly names the North Caucasus as the exception to its finding of no state-persecution risk elsewhere in Russia. For a visitor discovered or outed, the evidence indicates near-certain detention without legal process, torture, coerced conscription or death, with no functioning judicial remedy. This is approximately 0.11 below the national score of 0.12, reflecting a governance system where the state's security apparatus operates outside all legal constraint. Far below every other unit in the federation; even Dagestan and Ingushetia (0.04), which share the North Caucasus security logic, lack Chechnya's documented scale of extrajudicial killing and secret-prison infrastructure.

sources.title: Human rights group reports Chechen forces coercing detained gay men into military service, with at least seven sent to frontlines in Ukraine — The Insider
sources.claim_summary: The Insider (4 September 2024), reporting a human-rights group's documentation that Chechen security forces blackmail detained homosexual men into 'volunteering' for front-line service in Ukraine - at least seven sent, one already killed - a practice the dossier dates to before September 2022.

sources.title: Memorial investigation reveals Chechens are forcibly conscripted to fight in Ukraine
sources.claim_summary: OC Media report on a Memorial Human Rights Centre investigation: a mass wave of unlawful detentions in Chechnya tied to forced conscription for the war in Ukraine, following regional calls for Chechens to 'go to war'.

sources.title: Country policy and information note: sexual orientation and gender identity and expression, June 2025 (accessible) - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Home Office Country Policy and Information Note on sexual orientation and gender identity/expression (June 2025): LGBT+ people, including in Chechnya, form a particular social group; there is generally no real risk of state persecution elsewhere in Russia from sexual orientation alone, but people in the North Caucasus, trans people, and public LGBT+ advocates are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution; between 2017 and 2024 Chechen and North Caucasus authorities carried out systematic campaigns against LGBT+ people including abductions, torture and extrajudicial killings, and violence in detention spread beyond the Caucasus after the 2023 'extremist' designation.
